units.function: Tests Paperclip's responsible-user stamping for activity rows, including direct human actions and a fallback chain across heartbeat run, Issue, Agent API key, Company default and Issue creator.
units.dependencyDirection: The activity publication helper accepts actor/run/Issue/API-key context, reads operational tables through the database port, derives one responsibleUserId, persists it on ActivityLog and queues a post-commit publication.
units.keyDataModels: Activity actorType/actorId/action/entity, heartbeat run responsible user, Issue responsible user and creator, Agent API key responsible user, Company default responsible user and post-commit activity publication.
units.lifecycle: Human actions are attributed directly; Agent/system actions prefer explicit run attribution, then Issue attribution, then active API-key attribution, Company default and finally Issue creator. Malformed UUID-backed references are ignored, and the selected value is stamped when the activity row is written.
units.testAssessment: Nine focused cases exercise every fallback, malformed identifiers and one embedded-Postgres persistence path. Missing are tenant predicates on every lookup, inactive/revoked API keys, changed responsibility after run creation, null/unresolved attribution, transaction/publication failure, spoofed actor input, simultaneous contract changes, immutable history and distinction between initiator, observed actor, operator, approver and accountable human.
units.designRationale: Make Agent-originated activity explainable to a human operator even when the immediate actor is non-human, while preserving a compact column that audit views can filter.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must connect every executable action to its initiating principal and accountable human without losing the exact work, permission, data, approval, evidence and result context.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the ordered lookup as a best-effort operational attribution signal only. Store explicit, versioned ResponsibilityContract and WorkExecution references at authorization time; separately record observed actor, credential principal, initiating human, accountable human and approver. Unresolved attribution must remain explicit rather than silently becoming a Company default.
units.responsibilityConflict: A single inferred responsibleUserId conflates technical attribution with accepted organizational responsibility. Company default and Issue creator fallbacks can assign liability to someone who neither accepted the work nor approved the action, and later mutable table state is not proof of the contract effective when execution occurred.
evidence: 814cb336 allow agents to resolve review confirmations
b07b2994 stamp responsible users on activity logs

units.function: Route-level tests for Company activity, all-actor audit access tiers, Issue-run lookup, activity creation authorization and cross-tenant heartbeat-run existence-oracle resistance.
units.dependencyDirection: Express routes consume authenticated actor context and AccessService decisions, then call ActivityService, AgentActionAuditService, IssueService and HeartbeatService; the basic audit response is field-redacted before returning to the client.
units.keyDataModels: Company-scoped actor, access decision, audit actor scope/filter, activity attribution fields, Issue identifier, heartbeat run, list limit and basic/full response access tier.
units.lifecycle: A basic Company reader can inspect redacted all-actor events but cannot use attribution filters; an explicitly permitted reader receives full attribution. Company lists default to 100 and cap at 500. Issue identifiers are normalized before run lookup. Activity creation checks Company access. Cross-tenant and nonexistent run lookups both return 200 with an empty list, after anonymous callers are rejected, to avoid an existence oracle.
units.testAssessment: Nine route tests cover tiered disclosure, filter gating, limits, identifier resolution, write authorization and indistinguishable cross-tenant/not-found responses. Missing are cursor behavior for the ordinary activity endpoint, stable structured error codes, malformed/oversized filters, field-level policy evolution, response schema contracts, actor spoofing on create, rate limiting, CSRF, audit of denied queries, full middleware integration and leakage through timing or related entity fields.
units.designRationale: Offer a useful operational feed to broad Company readers while restricting sensitive Agent/run/human attribution, and prevent tenant membership probing through resource existence responses.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs separately governed operational status and responsibility evidence views, safe tenant boundaries and stable APIs consumable by its independent Web and Connector ecosystem.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the two-tier projection, filter authorization and indistinguishable existence response. Define policy-versioned field projections, cursor pagination, structured error codes and immutable access receipts. Separate a broad operational activity stream from the narrowly authorized ResponsibilityLedger rather than redacting one row shape ad hoc.
units.responsibilityConflict: The basic feed intentionally removes responsibleUserId, runId and details, so it cannot answer the product's responsibility-chain question. Conversely the full feed exposes raw details as a unit instead of applying data classification and purpose-bound field policy. The create surface is only shown checking Company access, not authority to assert the supplied actor/action/evidence semantics.

units.function: Embedded-Postgres tests for ordered activity listing, compact Issue-run ledger projections and asynchronous liveness backfill from run-bound comments and document revisions.
units.dependencyDirection: ActivityService reads ActivityLog, HeartbeatRun, Issue, comment and document/revision relations; it normalizes provider-shaped usage/results for API projection and can persist derived liveness fields back onto completed heartbeat runs.
units.keyDataModels: ActivityLog timestamp/action, heartbeat run context/usage/result/liveness/continuation, Issue status, run-bound Issue comment, document revision createdByRunId and continuation-summary document key.
units.lifecycle: Company activity is returned newest first with a limit. Issue-run views omit context snapshots and normalize a small allowlist of token, cost, billing and timeout fields. Completed runs missing liveness are classified and persisted; same-run concrete comments or document revisions can establish progress, while other-run revisions and continuation summaries are excluded and plan-only text stays non-evidence.
units.testAssessment: Five database integration cases validate ordering, payload compaction, persistence of a completed classification and two important false-positive exclusions. Missing are cursor pagination, deterministic ordering on timestamp ties, currency/provider provenance, invalid/negative/overflow usage, redaction of secrets in allowed fields, concurrent backfill, failure retry, immutable source hashes, deleted/edited comments, artifact/evidence authorization, all liveness classes and proof that classification changes cannot rewrite historical accountability.
units.designRationale: Keep the Issue run ledger fast and bounded despite arbitrary provider payloads, and repair older or incomplete runs using concrete artifacts instead of trusting an Agent's prose summary as proof of progress.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs efficient run projections and a defensible separation between self-reported status, observable work activity, evidence artifacts and final responsibility records.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the allowlisted payload projection, exact run binding and exclusion of continuation summaries. Keep liveness as a recomputable operational projection with classifier version and source references. Evidence admission must instead create immutable, content-addressed Evidence records with origin, authorization, retention and verification state; cost needs currency, provider and pricing provenance.
units.responsibilityConflict: Backfilled liveness mutates the run record and labels comments/revisions as concrete action evidence without an immutable admission receipt or accountable reviewer. It is a useful health inference, not proof that the authorized goal was satisfied, the data use was permitted or the result was approved. Compact cost fields also lose enough provenance to be unsuitable for contractual accounting.
